reason: The basket seems useful for collecting the potato crop, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect to lift the potatoes from the trough into the basket, though I don't know what the harvest will look like.

effect: The harvest is ready, and the new goal is to taste it.
reaction: Seeing the potatoes grow larger than the seed pieces is satisfying, especially after the storm.
reason: The galley has what I need to prepare the potatoes, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect to wash and cook the potatoes for a meal, though I don't know exactly how they'll be prepared.

effect: The potatoes became a cooked meal, completing the harvest goal and the chapter.
reaction: The quiet radio hiss makes the meal feel solitary after the long effort to keep the crop alive.

mostWorthwhile.text: Lifting the potatoes was most worthwhile: seeing a substantial crop emerge made the time and care invested in the trough feel tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Preparing the meal was straightforward and left little choice, although the quiet scene was evocative.

surprise.text: The potatoes were larger than the seed pieces brought from Earth; I had not known what the harvest would look like.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: the basket suited the harvest, and the galley suited preparing it.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I want to learn what happens to the specimens and the journey home; this chapter's quiet meal also made the expedition feel personal.
